title: AI Chatbots as Multi-Role Pedagogical Agents: Transforming Engagement in CS Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses challenges in computer science education, including low student engagement, high student-to-teacher ratios, limited personalized feedback, and students’ reluctance to participate in inquiry-based learning. The authors position AI chatbots, particularly large language model-based pedagogical agents, as a potential solution for improving engagement, motivation, and the quality of student inquiry in CS learning environments.

The proposed intervention is a multi-role chatbot learning environment composed of four pedagogical agents: an Instructor Bot for academic guidance, a Peer/Social Companion Bot for collaborative and social interaction, a Career Advising Bot for connecting coursework to future careers, and an Emotional Supporter Bot for affective support. A chatbot manager routes student queries to the most suitable bot. The study is framed as design-based research and uses an ABC experimental structure comparing three conditions: human tutor instruction, a single chatbot, and a multi-role chatbot. Data collection includes interaction logs, surveys, focus groups, and NLP-based analyses such as topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and sequence analysis.

The target population is approximately 200 postgraduate computer science students at a higher education institution in Germany, with random allocation to the three study conditions. The intervention is planned to last one month. The broader context is CS education, with some references to data science courses and CS1 support in the pilot findings.

The paper’s main conclusions are preliminary rather than definitive. Pilot results suggest that large language model-based chatbots can generate accurate, fluent, relevant, and human-like responses to student questions, with stronger engagement and empathy for higher-order cognitive questions. The authors conclude that multi-role AI chatbots show promise as tools for creating more engaging, supportive, and personalized learning experiences in computer science education, though the paper mainly presents a research design and early pilot evidence rather than full outcome results from the main study.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used as a conversational pedagogical chatbot.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the underlying LLM for a proposed multi-role pedagogical chatbot system in CS education, including Instructor Bot, Peer/Social Companion Bot, Career Advising Bot, and Emotional Supporter Bot; preliminary pilot evaluated LLM-generated answers to student questions for accuracy, fluency, empathy, engagement, and relevance.

findings.finding_summary: In a pilot evaluation, the LLM was reported to provide accurate and human-like responses to student questions in a CS1 context. Semantic similarity and keyword co-occurrence analyses were said to indicate relevance and coherence of responses, but no effect sizes, inferential statistics, or sample size were reported.
findings.measure: Quality of LLM-generated Q&A responses, including accuracy, fluency, and relevance based on expert screening, ground-truth checking, semantic similarity, and keyword co-occurrence analysis

findings.finding_summary: The chatbot showed higher engagement and empathy for questions at higher cognitive levels than for questions at lower cognitive levels in the pilot study. The paper does not report numeric differences, effect sizes, or the number of evaluated interactions.
findings.measure: Empathy and engagement of chatbot responses across Bloom's taxonomy cognitive levels

quality_tier_rationale: Although the paper proposes an experimental design, the reported evidence is only preliminary pilot output evaluation with no clear sample size, no reported statistical testing, and limited methodological detail for empirical outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings are described as promising and positive, but impact is unclear because no effect sizes, confidence intervals, or student outcome gains are reported.
